world_states.name: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player
Cannibal Grand Wizard imprisoned by player

say: Smell that? Smoke, and something sweeter under it.
The grass here grows too well. I won't be thinking about why.
Bones lined up in rows. Rows. Somebody has a system.
I've killed forty men and I'm still not ready for this place.
The wind stinks of woodsmoke and the wrong kind of cooking. Keep moving.
Walk in the middle. Nobody falls behind. Nobody.
Nobody takes the rear alone. Nobody sleeps first. That's the whole plan.
If one of us is dragged off, the rest keep walking. I mean it. I'll do the same.
Spread out and they pick one. Bunch up and they pick two.
Hands near your weapons, mouths shut. Let the grass do the talking.
Eyes up. Every ridge has someone on it and none of them are waving.
Drag your boots and they hear you. Lift them and they smell you.
I swear I saw painted faces in the grass. Gone when I looked again.
The old hands said never sleep on this ground. I thought they were being dramatic.
Whoever is out there has been tracking us since the last ridge. They're just patient.
Please. Please can we go round. There must be a round.
I hear drums. No. That's my heart. Let it be my heart.
My mother told me tales about these plains to make me eat my greens. They were too mild.
If I faint, don't leave me here. If I die, do leave me. I mean it. Burn nothing.
I thought the stories were exaggerated. I'd be happy to be wrong about the stories.
I'm not going to be sick. I'm going to be sick.
If I start screaming, someone slap me. Gently. Then run.
Don't leave me behind. I'm not much use, but I'd be an awful meal.
Is it supposed to smell like roast? In the middle of the afternoon? Why does it smell like roast?
I want to go home. I have wanted to go home for six miles.
Flatskins of the Plains aren't warriors. They're hunger with a spear. I won't call it honour.
A Shek dies in battle or in the sand. Not in a pot. Don't let me end in a pot.
The Stone Golem looks away from this ground.
Honour is a sword in the open. Here they eat the sword, and then the swordsman, and then the sheath.
Even Kral's Chosen would walk around. I'm walking around. We're all walking around.
If we are taken, whoever lives, remember the sound of the drums.
Keep your blade bare and your voice low. Honour is no use against a cooking pot.
Remember: if they get me, burn the body. I don't wish to be served.
A Shek dies on his feet. Here, a Shek dies on a spit. I would rather the first.
We came as warriors. We shall leave as warriors. Or we shall not leave.
The drones in the south wouldn't speak of this. Now I understand the silence.
So many bodies, and none of them rest. They're carried away. We mustn't be carried.
You can smell them on the wind. Hungry.
The song of the drones was always a comfort. Here the song is a scream stretched thin. I can't find the end of it.
I tasted blood in my mouth the moment we crossed. I haven't bitten my tongue.
They won't eat me. They'll do something worse: ignore me while they eat you.
My frame isn't food. Remarkably, I feel no relief.
Smoke, fat and burnt hair detected. Conclusion: don't stand downwind.
Their teeth are for flesh and my frame isn't flesh. I'd still rather the rest of you stayed close.
Skeleton frames aren't on their menu. They hunt us for sport.
Something in the soil is laughing. Something fed. Something with a mouth in it.
The red here's old. It has been fed for years and it wants a little more.
Nice weather for it. Whatever it is. Do you hear them? The grass is making room for something.
The soil is red in a way soil shouldn't be. It has been taught to want things.
The wind laughs low in the grass. It has forgotten how to laugh any other way.
Don't look at the horizon. The horizon is looking at you.
Keep your eyes on your feet.
I smell a dinner being planned. Nobody tell the ones who are the dinner.
Don't answer the voices in the grass. They ask nicely.
Something old lives under all of this.
Count heads. Don't count the ones on poles.
Boots in the dust, small ones. They didn't leave by walking.
Birds won't land here. That tells me what the birds know.
Why is every second hut empty and every third one hung with bells? Do not answer.
I hear music. A flute. A thin one. Made of something long and hollow.
Hands off your weapons until I say, but be ready. If they come low in the grass, we do not talk. We run, then we fight.
Rope him short. If he stumbles, he drags us all. Cut him loose before you let him drag us.
Nobody talks to him. Nobody gives him water. If he's quiet, we're all quiet.
If it comes to a chase, he goes in the bushes. I am sorry. I do not like it either.
He's worth good money, and the Plains would pay in bones.
Whoever you tied up is shaking so hard the rope sings. Even he knows where we are.
He wakes and sobs and sleeps. Better than the other thing. The other thing being what is coming for him.
He's tied and he's awake. I wish he weren't. I wish I weren't.
Make sure the knots hold. If he runs, he leads them to us.
They'll smell a bound man across the whole plain.
Please, no, not here, anywhere but here. Cut me loose, I'll walk, I'll run, I'll carry your bags.
This is the place. This is where they take you. Put me down. Put me DOWN.
I heard them talk about the plains in the cage. I'm not going in alive. Kill me first, please, kill me first.
You're carrying me to the Plains. I know it. Whatever you're paid, I'll double it. Triple.
I can't feel my hands. I can't feel anything but the smell. Is it burning? Is it me?
Darkfinger. The finger that points at your grave.
Villages along this spit aren't villages. They're kitchens with roofs.
If we find the First Village, we look, we don't touch, we leave.
I once saw a tree here with fruit. Hands. Dozens of hands.
Don't eat the berries, don't drink the stream, don't accept hospitality, don't accept anything.
I said it as a joke. It wasn't a joke.
It was not a joke the first time either. Move on.
I'll laugh later. I'll laugh when we're far away.
Don't read the gate signs. Don't read any of them.
Everyone take a deep breath. Now never take one this deep again.
The Hunters said this peninsula never stops giving. They meant corpses, I think.
A cook fire in daylight. Nobody sane lights one here unless the meat is fresh.
Cook smoke on three sides. They're making dinner for a hundred and not a single table.
Hunters have a saying, if you hear laughter, run towards the sea.
Every doorway on this peninsula has a hand nailed up beside it.
That isn't pork. Don't smell it again.
Don't let a child approach you. Whatever it asks, the answer is no.
The pots are always on the fire here. Remember that when someone offers you stew.
Count the exits. There is one, behind us. They know it.
Don't accept gifts. A fish is a hook, a bone is a hook, everything is a hook.
There are skulls on the gate. Little ones too. Little ones.
I want to go home. I want any home. A cellar, a drain, anywhere not here.
I feel eyes on my back like hot irons. I'm not turning round. I'm going to keep walking and keep praying.
Gate posts decorated with fingers. Fingers! I counted twelve and made myself stop.
Even the stones are warm. Why are the stones warm? I don't want to know.
Kral never claimed this ground, and now I see he was wise.
Flatskins living off flatskins. A shame with no name.
No Shek has come here to die. It would be too dishonourable, and too crowded.
If I fall here, take my blade home. Don't leave it for them to polish.
This is a place where honour has been eaten. Let us not be the next course.
Don't pity them. Pity makes you slow.
The old songs say a warrior fears nothing. The old songs never came here.
Keep close and keep your hands busy. Idle hands tempt idle mouths.
Don't insult them. Don't reason with them. Don't turn your back.
I'd rather face a hundred honest foes than one of these grinning faces.
The ground hums with chewing. Not an animal.
Our hive kept the old stories of tribes like this. We hoped they were stories.
The tribes keep hives of their own, of a sort. They call them villages. They don't hum, they chew.
The ground is full of old voices. They don't sing.
Hold hands, friends. The smoke on the wind isn't a kindness.
Skull count at village gate: seventeen. Several recent. Several sized for children.
Recommendation: don't stop. Don't sleep. Don't accept supper. Don't discuss what we saw at the gate.
Preliminary count: forty-one hanging objects within sight. Human origin confirmed in thirty-eight.
Smoke is detected on three bearings. Fat content in the smoke is elevated.
Door lintels carved with tally marks. Tally exceeds my ability to count in the time available.
Shapes crawl between the huts on all fours and rise when we look. Good game.
The ground here's warm, with a smell like a hearth that has been burning for centuries.
Everyone here's smiling, and I can't find the source of the joke.
The hearths are always lit. Always.
The shadows between the huts are the wrong shape. They keep the shape of people crouching.
This place wants us to be afraid, and it's working, so well done.
Don't touch the hanging things. Don't look at the hanging things. Don't ask what they were.
Look at the paint on the doorframes. It's red and it's wet.
Somebody is humming a lullaby. It's a nice lullaby. It stops each time I turn.
Do not drink the water. Do not look in the water. If the water looks back, drink nothing.
He can't stop crying through the gag. Good. Let him cry, but do it quietly, for all our sakes.
Mind your captive. Cannibals prize a fresh prisoner. We're close enough that he can smell the pot.
Don't look at him. If he sees a face he knows, he will cry out. Then we all cry out.
He knows this place. He knew it before we told him. That is the worst thing about him.
If they offer to buy him, we say no. If they offer to take him, we say we aren't selling.
This is where they put people in cages. I have seen them, from far. Don't take me closer, please, don't take me closer.
Is that smoke the cooking pits? Is it? Oh no.
The First Village. I know it from the whispers. Take me back. Take me back and I will tell you anything, anything.
I can feel the heat of the fires from here. I know what's in the fires. Don't go closer.
They have a pit in the middle. I have never seen it. I have heard it, in my dreams.
The fishermen up here sleep in shifts and call it fishing.
They say the painted ones wade out at low tide. I choose to believe that's a joke.
The coast is a lie. The sea looks like an escape. The sea is only a longer road to the same grave.
Smoke from the Plains to the south, all day. Every day.
The beach is full of footprints. All bare. All leading inland.
I'll take the first watch. I'll take the second. I won't be sleeping.
Never stand with the sea behind you. Never stand with the land behind you.
One of us sleeps, three of us wake. We rotate, even if it kills us.
Keep your boots dry. Wet feet slow you down. Slow gets you cooked.
If you see a lantern bobbing on the water, it isn't a fisherman.
Deadcat folk keep their doors barred and their children counted. Sensible people.
Hunters come this way to cull the tribes. Good luck to them. Bad luck to us if they fail.
Cold water on the left, cold stares on the right. Pick your side.
Hunters patrol this coast, so the tribes know there are still those who object.
The locals do not even look at us. That is how they survive, by looking at nobody.
A whole town lost to the plains, and these are what's left. Shells of people, holding lanterns.
Nobody will meet my eyes. I think they're counting who they'll lose next.
The tide leaves things on the beach. Usually shells. Today a boot, with the foot still in it.
I want to cry and I won't. A fisherman's wife just watched me with the eyes of a drowned woman.
I heard someone whispering my name from the water. I do not know anyone out there.
Stay close. Hold my sleeve if you must. I won't say a word.
Stay in the light. Stay where they can see you. Stay where I can see you.
Don't touch anything on the beach. Not the shells. Not the rope.
I want to go back to a town with walls. I want a wall.
Everyone has a child they've lost. That's how you know where you are.
A coast should be wide and free. This one is a keyhole with someone watching through it.
I haven't seen one sea-bird. Not one. Even the gulls have fled.
A Shek would have settled this coast with swords.
The people here bar their doors against the Plains. A Shek would have taken the fight to them.
A coast that fears the land and the land that fears the coast.
We are far from the Queen. Far from any queen.
The fishermen's nets look wrong, too large for fish. I do not wish to think what for.
The fishing nets carry no fish, only salt and old hair. I have no words for that.
The tide pulls like a mouth. The sand whispers in all the wrong voices.
Salt wind and old smoke. Even the gulls carry the smell of something cooked.
Sea, sand, ash. Cannibal tracks at the tide line. Fresh. Keep this in mind when sleeping.
Several sets of bare footprints near the water's edge. Fresh. Six. They go out. They don't come back.
Tide pattern inconsistent with local activity. Footprints enter the water.
Smoke detected seaward and inland simultaneously. Don't trust either direction.
Bare footprints, six sets, converging on the waterline. The newest are very recent.
The waves keep bringing back the same bone. It's waiting for something.
The salt hurts. The wind hurts. Everything here's a small, polite violence.
The sea here has teeth. It has been practising on the shore for ten thousand years.
The foam on the waves has a pattern. It's spelling something. I won't read it.
I can smell the smoke before I see it. The sea can't wash the smell from the air.
Don't wander off to relieve yourself. Take two people. Take three.
Don't light anything at dusk. Sleep without fire, if you must sleep. If you can.
Do not stand silhouetted against the water. Do not stand silhouetted against anything.
Anything that washes up here belongs to someone. Don't take it. They'll come for it.
Keep your bags between you and the dunes. If something grabs, let it grab the bag.
He keeps staring inland. Good eyes. He knows what's out there. We're only passing, friend, only passing.
If the sea gets quiet, they're coming. If it gets loud, they're coming.
He keeps looking at the water. I think he's hoping for a boat.
If he calls out, they will hear it on the whole coast. Hold something over his mouth.
Whatever we do with him, we do it before dark.
I know this coast. Boats don't leave from here, they flee. Don't leave me here, I beg you.
I won't run. I won't run. I won't run. My legs are running anyway, if you would please put them down.
This coast is where they sell people. I know it. I've heard it in the ports.
I'll do anything. I'll carry your pack, I'll cook your meals. Don't leave me on this shore.
The tide is coming in. I can hear it. I can hear them coming in with it.
Nice name for a place where something eats you in private.
Trees this thick, you could be dragged off and nobody turns round.
The ninjas keep this place secret for a reason. The reason isn't their own safety.
Someone cooked here, recently, with the big pots. Don't look in the pots. Don't look.
The trees are too close together. It's by design. Something wants us in single file.
Keep your voices low and your weapons lower. Loud things are noticed.
If one of us goes silent, we stop. If two of us go silent, we run.
The paths bend wrong. They lead back on themselves. Trust nothing that looks like a trail.
Stay out of the shadows. Stay out of the light. Stay between, where the dark is thin.
Don't shoot at noises. Noises are bait. Shoot only at what shoots at you.
The ninjas hole up here because the painted tribes keep their own enemies busy. Think about what that says.
Branches creak wrong. Like they carry weight.
Pine needles don't crackle if someone has walked here a thousand times. That's how I know someone has.
Whoever lives here has eaten everything that used to. Not a rabbit, not a bird.
The undergrowth is trampled in a perfect line. Someone walks this route often, in step.
Why is it so quiet? Birds should sing. Birds have learned something we haven't.
Please let me stay in the middle. I don't care if I carry all the bags.
I keep thinking I hear singing. It stops when I listen. It starts again when I stop.
I keep tripping on things and I don't look down. I'd rather not know.
Even the moss is trampled. Someone has been walking here in bare feet.
I won't cry. I won't cry.
If something touches my shoulder, I'll scream.
Every tree looks like a person standing very still. That is a stupid thought. I cannot stop it.
I counted us twice. We were one more than before. I counted again. We were right.
Don't leave me with the pack. Don't leave me alone.
No sand, no sky, no honest fight. A trapper's country. I dislike it.
No honourable foe makes his lair in a forest like this.
A forest isn't a battlefield. A forest is where cowards plan their ambush.
I would rather fight in the open sun than in this smothering green.
A warrior who hides in trees is no warrior. A man who hunts from them is worse.
The pines whisper and the whisper is made of feet. Many feet, and slow, so slow.
The trees grow close together and the roots wrap one another. They've eaten too, in their way.
The forest smells of old fear. The bark remembers every scream and keeps it.
The trees are full of eyes that are not eyes. Soft ones. Many soft ones.
I hear many soft footfalls above us. They follow at our pace and make no sound but breath.
Heat signatures at the margins. Four. Six. Stationary. They're waiting for the light to change.
Heat shadows. Many. Motionless. They keep within the tree line and they keep their breath slow.
Observation: leaf litter disturbed in a ring around our position. Radius forty metres.
Estimate: twelve to eighteen hostiles in the tree line. They haven't moved in some time.
Detected: elevated body heat at multiple canopy positions. Observation continues. They watch us as we watch them.
Something smiled at me from the trees. It had too many teeth for the face it wore.
The pines are leaning to watch us pass. Bow politely.
Branches bend toward us as we pass. They're being polite. It makes the skin crawl.
The needles smell of blood washed with rain. It's the best this forest can do.
The wind in the branches sounds like whispering. The whispering is almost words.
Stay on the path. If the path leaves you, you leave the path.
Don't eat what you find hanging. Don't eat anything. I won't be explaining.
Don't climb the trees. There's a reason the pines are bare below the knee.
Don't pick anything up. Not a coin, not a boot. Someone left it for a reason.
If a branch cracks behind you, don't turn. Keep going and count to ten.
Hush him. If he screams in these woods, we're lunch for whoever hears it.
We stop for a moment only, and nobody leaves his boots. Anything left on the ground tonight won't be found.
He isn't struggling any more. That's worse. A quiet man in a forest is a dinner bell.
Tie his hands to the rope, not to each other. If we are jumped, I can cut him loose.
The ninjas won't help. The tribes won't wait. He's on his own and so are we.
They take people into forests like this one. I was almost taken once. Please, no.
I have seen this forest from the inside of a sack, once. It was no better. Please hand me back to the Hunters.
I know these trees. They're the ones with the ropes. Please don't take me in among the ropes.
They hang people here by the feet. I saw one once, from a boat.
Take me back to the road. I'll go anywhere you want, only not into the dark.
Name says it all. Skinners. Somebody up there's measuring us for a coat.
Every rock here could hide a knife. Every knife here has done this before.
I'd rather be eaten. At least that ends.
Hide in the stone folds and the wind tells you nothing.
Wind sounds like someone sharpening something. Do you hear it? Do you hear it.
Every rock casts a shadow with arms. I know it's the rocks.
Back to back at night. Skin isn't a thing you get back.
Watch your own shadow. It can be cut free more easily than you think.
If we're taken, we aren't taken quietly. Agreed? Agreed.
Keep the lamps low and the voices lower. We're being read like a pattern.
No one wanders off. The Roam is tidy and it doesn't like loose ends.
Corpses with no skin look like red statues. Found three already. They won't be the last.
Hunger I can face. A knife that does its work slow, with a smile? Not in my line.
Their victims don't scream long. They save their breath to ask a single question: why me.
I carry a vial. If they take me, I drink it. That isn't a joke. Don't ask for a taste.
Hang a bell on the sentry. The Roam doesn't like noise. It loves to correct it.
Do they know we're here? They know. Tell me they don't.
I have soft skin. The softest. Oh, no, I didn't mean that as a boast.
Skin first, then muscle, then bone. None of it goes back on.
I can't stop thinking about the sound. I've never heard it, and I can't stop.
Someone just spoke very kindly behind that rock. Nobody was there. It was a kind voice.
I have decided to be very ugly from now on.
If a stranger offers to measure you, say no. Say no, and keep saying it.
I put on three coats. It won't help but it makes me feel better.
I keep thinking about my own hands. They're good hands. I'd like to keep them.
Every rock on this road looks like a person kneeling. Don't look at the rocks.
A Shek is proud of his scars. Here they're what they take first.
Honour says fight. Wisdom says run. Both say don't be taken alive.
A Shek's sword arm is his pride. They would take it first, and wear it as a sleeve.
We won't run, we'll fight. And if we're taken, we won't scream. I'll hold you to that.
A Shek gives his hide to the sand in the end.
We bury our own, here, with their skins on.
Don't let them touch your face. Face is all a Shek has left.
If I die, bury me deep and burn the top. Leave nothing they can sew.
Our blades are good. Our nerves are better. Remember that when the quiet starts.
I'll fall before I scream. I'll scream before I yield. I'll yield before I'm skinned.
I felt a thing in the dust. Not wind. Many cold feet, in rhythm. They walk like they have all night.
The hive remembers the old stories of the thin ones. The tall metal ones who make cloth from flesh. I thought the stories were exaggerated.
Wherever we go, I feel the dust on my face as though it were a hand.
The air hums thin and dry. It's the hum of a held breath and a long needle.
Quiet little ones, hold hands. The hive reaches thin here, and the cloth wants us.
Skeletons, here. In human hides. This is what the Holy Nation screams about. They're right for once.
I don't know whose skin they wear. I know I could ask the skin.
A skeleton in a human face. I want to talk to it. I don't want to talk to it. Both are true.
It isn't easy to be a skeleton in this part of the world. I note that it isn't easy.
The shapes on the ridge walk like us. They're wrong in a way I don't like to name.
The dust has a smell like new leather. I didn't know leather had a smell until now.
I see a pair of eyes in the red rock. They aren't eyes. They're holes. Someone has cut very neatly.
The red cliffs are polished smooth, as if from being rubbed with something.
Everything is dry and clean. The dust is swept. Who sweeps the dust?
The rocks have been scraped clean in strips, as if by someone with a very thin knife.
Look, there. A shape on the ridge, wearing a face that isn't its own. Don't wave.
The abandoned mines up here are empty of tools. Full of leather scraps.
A very, very quiet man waved to us from a ridge, then went behind a rock. We haven't seen him since. Neither have we seen the rock move.
Nobody sleeps in the same spot twice. Move the camp every night. Move it before you think.
The tracks here lead one way. No one has ever come back along them.
They will not take me from the front. They never do.
They always pick the one who's thinking about something else.
Count your fingers. Count them again. Keep counting until we're out.
The ones that smile are the ones I trust least. Which is all of them.
They won't come at us while we're all together. They'll wait.
Whatever happens, he lives or dies with his skin on. I want that clear. The skinners can have nothing.
His skin, his skin, his skin. Look after his skin. Remember we have to give it back whole.
He won't wake up for another hour. Good. If he wakes here, he will think of nothing else.
Don't let him see the ridge. He will start to count the skins.
If they want him, they'll take him, and us with him. Keep him hidden under the cloak.
The roam. They come in the night with machines. I have heard the machines. Please, not me, please.
If you hand me over here, I'll haunt you, I swear it. Leather and bone.
Please. Skin is the one thing I've never lent to anyone. Please. Don't lend it now.
I can hear needles. Quiet little clicks in the rocks.
Don't take me closer. I've heard what happens to those who go through the front door.
Quiet down. Sound carries in the dark and the sound I fear is a drum of hide.
This is the end of the road, the place nobody comes back from. Plenty went in.
If the skinners have a home, we're walking onto its mat.
The dark has a hum and the hum has a tune. I'm humming it. Oh, no. I'm humming it.
No fires. Nobody lights a fire. No. Fires show them where the softest ones are.
I did not mean to say that aloud.
Not a word. Not a breath.
Look at the doors, not the windows.
Follow the footprints we left. Not the ones we find.
No lights. They love lights. They collect them.
A house of skins. I heard the tale in three taverns and laughed in all of them. I am not laughing.
Tools on a table, shined. Somebody cares for their tools. That's the worst thing I've seen today.
Leather tied in neat bundles beside the road. Sorted by size. I do not want to guess the sizes.
Quality work, at a glance. Even stitches. A craftsman is somewhere ahead.
The quiet here isn't empty. It's full and polite and waiting.
Keep your boots on. Keep your gloves on.
If anyone calls you by name, they aren't your friend. Don't answer to your name.
The air has a smell like a clean stable, and the stable is very large.
Don't trust the cleanest road. The cleanest road is the one they made.
Boots, belts, buckles. Check each one. Check them for anyone else's name.
Why would anyone make clothes from... I can't finish that.
The air is so still. It listens. Don't talk.
I won't touch the doors. I won't open the doors. Whatever is behind them isn't for me.
Why is everything so tidy? The dust is swept. The hooks are polished.
I can smell oil. Leather oil. Someone has been oiling something. Oiling it well.
I have cut through men in the Stenn and not blinked. A man who cuts to wear is another thing. A thing without a name.
The old Shek say a coward flees the dark and a fool walks into it. I intend to be a coward very quickly.
If my body is found without its skin, tell my kin I died with my sword in my hand.
This isn't a dark a warrior can fight. It's a dark that sews you in.
In the Stenn I knew every enemy by his smell. Here I smell only neat, tidy work.
Even the drones of the south speak in whispers about this ground. They know what comes over the border.
Even our Southern kin hold their breath along this border. We watch them and they watch us and nobody exhales.
Machines hum, nothing living does. I miss the thread of my kin like a lost tooth.
The hum of the south is faint, like a lullaby from the next valley. This place is silent as a sealed jar.
I cannot hear my own heart. The dark has taken it for a bolt of cloth.
Warning: ahead are my relatives, in a manner of speaking. Don't mention it. I won't.
Cousins in the dark. Cousins in cloth. I feel no kinship. I feel the opposite of kinship. A new word is needed.
Sound level is anomalously low. Interpretation: engineered silence.
Ahead, the architecture is familiar. It was designed for storage. I decline to state what's stored.
I'm cold. This is odd. I don't usually feel cold. I note it. I wish I hadn't.
They don't know you're one of the quiet kind, brother.
They won't take the brother who's already a brother of the dark.
Walk in my footsteps. If the floor gives, it gives under me first.
I can't tell the difference between the dark and the cloth. I suspect there's none.
If I'm taken, don't come for me. If I'm dismantled, don't collect the parts.
Layers. They wear layers. Each layer a person. I can feel them breathing under the cloth.
The dark has a skin of its own. It's thinner than I expected. It's going to rip.
The silence is stitched. You can see the seams if you look straight at it.
I see threads hanging from the roof of the dark. They're moving.
Every echo returns a little too late, as though it stopped to look at us.
If they take me, stitch my name somewhere you can read it. I want somebody to know.
Let nobody go to relieve himself without a cord tied round him. A cord, a cord, a cord.
If you hear a machine, the machine is the least dangerous thing in the room.
The doors are too well hung. They open without a sound.
Don't step into pools of light. Light is how they choose.
Look at him. He knows. He knows what this place does to people like him. We should have left him on the road.
It won't be worth the trouble. A man who has been through this isn't worth much on the market. I'm sorry.
He knows where we're headed. He kept quiet till now. He has started to shake.
If he screams, it will carry. If it carries, they will come to meet it.
I don't like how he looks at the gates. He looks at them like a man who has been before.

The spiders here are bigger than men. The webs are bigger than the spiders. Nobody tells us the rest.
Somebody has strung a trap across the whole valley. The thread catches the light.
Watch the ground and the sky.
Never step in a straight line. Never step in a rhythm. They hear a march.
If one of us sticks, the rest cut and go. Don't hesitate.
Watch the walls. Watch the ceiling. Watch the web. Watch the spiders. Watch your feet.
Keep your hand on your knife. A web is a rope, and ropes can be cut.
A thousand legs tapping in the dark. Not a plan. Not an army.
Every footstep is a pulse down the web. A thousand legs, listening. Be careful where you put your feet.
The legs are the size of tree trunks. They tap, tap, tap in the dark. The dark is much larger than it should be.
Don't touch the silk. Don't even breathe on it.
Be quiet, be quick, and be unmemorable. Spiders only remember the loud.
Webs as thick as sails. Don't touch the webs. Don't look at what's in the webs.
I thought it was a cobweb. It was a rope, with someone on the end of it.
Is that a man in the silk? Don't answer. Don't look. I looked.
I've never been so afraid of the ceiling.
Don't make me look up. Please don't make me look up.
Don't make a sound. Please don't make a sound.
If a strand touches my face, I will scream. Fair warning. I will scream and then run.
The sticky ones are over there. The silent ones are over there. Where are the harmless ones?
I do not have a plan for this. I never had a plan for this. I have never planned for anything.
They're coming. I can hear them coming. Why are they coming so slowly?
The Bugmaster has sat on his throne for centuries. I have no wish to see what he eats.
The throne of the Bugmaster is a legend. Legends should stay in the mouths of drunks.
A king of vermin on a throne of bones. A fitting home for a thing with no honour.
The Bugmaster's legend frightens even those who laugh at legends.
Shek don't flee the dark. Shek leave it, by choice, in good order.
Insect minds. Hungry. Patient. I know the cold of them and I want to forget.
Not a mind. A hunger with legs. I can't reach it. I hope I never can.
The spiders speak in a clicking that bores into the mind. It's a language of hunger.
Their dreams are mean little things, hungry in a hundred directions. I wish I could not hear.
The web hums beneath our feet. The hum is the hive's cousin, and its enemy.
Nothing returns from the throne. Probability of our returning: low. Probability of our being wrapped: high.
No heat, no breath, no heartbeat. I'm nearly invisible. I'm also, unfortunately, nearly alone.
Webs detected at height of four metres, strand thickness consistent with load-bearing.
Biological inventory: spiders, various. Dead, wrapped: eleven. Alive, wrapped: four.
I'll go first. If I'm caught, you may use me as a tool for cutting silk.
Eight legs, eight eyes, one idea. The idea is us.
The silk has a smell like a freshly opened grave.
Eight eyes of purple fire in the cavern roof. They aren't blinking. They aren't hungry.
The silk is warm. The silk is alive.
Everything is a web. Even the dark is a web.
Hold the line and keep your feet quiet. The web remembers every step.
Spread out. A web catches a crowd. A hunter picks a straggler.
Walk where I walk. Step where I step. If the ground sags, the ground isn't ground.
The last party through here sent back one man. He didn't speak.
Never go back for a dropped item. The dropped item is bait.
He will be bait if we have to. I'm sorry. I didn't want to say it.
He's meat on a leash. I'm sorry. If the spiders come, I'll cut the leash.
He's wriggling. Stop that. Every wriggle is a message. The web hears messages.
If we leave him tied, he's a lure. If we take him, he's a rope. Either way, he's spiders' business.
I can't trust him to keep still. Gag him and sit on him.
Please, not the webs. Not the spiders. I can't bear the little legs.
Spiders feed on the still ones. If they catch me, I'll be so still.
Please tell me we aren't going in. I've heard what they do with the still ones.
The webs are hung with the ones who tried to escape. I can't be one of those.
I'd rather be a slave. I'd rather be cattle.
Gran' Wizard say stew simmer till moon. Moon already up. /CANNIBALHA/.
No waste. Skin make drum. Bone make spoon. Spoon feed little one.
Count cages. Count again. One missing.
Tonight we /CANNIBALCOOK/ long one, red hair. Tomorrow short one.
Dream Plains is one big mouth. Wake up, I ungry.
Meat Lord eat first. Dhen Chiefs. Dhen rest. Dhen dogs. Dhis week I eat after dogs.
/CANNIBALCURSE/! New one bite me. I bite back. Now we friends.
No name meat. Name make meat sad. Sad meat /CANNIBALTOUGH/.
New one cry. I say good. Tears is salt. Save for pot.
Tonight I head of circle. Tomorrow I arm. Next week I bowl. Dhat how it turn.
Traders come up from south. So nice. So round. We keep dhem for winter.
Hunters out again, dhey say. I put out more bowl.
Everybody say we mean. We not mean. We ungry.
Man come, ask what in pot. Now he is pot. Funny, no? /CANNIBALHA/.
Hunters wear red. Red not show blood.
My knife have name. Long name. Name of everybody I meet.
No more dig grave. Waste shovel.
Last tooth-puller, we eat in spring. Taste like clove.
Wizard say patience. Belly say no patience.
Dhey say we animal. Animal eat what it find. We choose.
Meat! Meat walk! /CANNIBALHA/ /CANNIBALHA/! Bring big pot!
You look /CANNIBALSOFT/. We gentle. First bite most gentle.
/CANNIBALCURSE/! Resh ones! We so ungry, and you come so kind.
I take leg. Who take head? Say now, before fight.
Hee hee! Runner! Love runner. Runner sweat salt on self.
Run! Please run! Chase is half flavour!
Wizard say no play with food. I play little.
Look at haunch on dhat one! Mmmm!
Run, little meat! Run, make self tender!
/CANNIBALCURSE/! He have sword. I take sword after hand.
Your /CANNIBALBODYPART/ be feast. Sorry. No, not sorry.
Skin so clean. Soon not clean.
Belly sing about you long time. Keep still. I want hear end of song.
Bones! Look at bones! Marrow like butter. I see it in walk.
Cut at knee, he stop. Cut at neck, he stop forever. Choose!

say: Visitor! Sit! Sit! Room by fire.
Hee hee. You walk like good marrow. Come to village.
You smell /CANNIBALTASTY/. I mean clean. I mean friend. /CANNIBALHA/.
No be scared. We good host. Ask last ones. Cannot.
Hello, hello, meat! Walk with us! Short walk.
Stranger have price. Everybody have. Today, you.
We no say no to guest. We say yes.
We have fire! We have pot! Pot have room.
No walk away. Grass longer dhan you dhink.
Strangers! Village wait long time for strangers! Come, quick, before stew cold.
Down! He down! Pick up, pick up, careful of /CANNIBALBODYPART/!
Sleeping one! Quiet, quiet. Tie first. Wake him in cage.
/CANNIBALHA/! Free dinner! Who drop him? Who drop him get smallest piece.
Ahh! Sleeper! Snoring meal! Carry gentle, or juice spoil.
He out like candle. Light him again in cage.
Still warm. Warm is best. Hurry hurry hurry.
Dead? No? Good. Dead go bad. Alibe keep in cage till thaw.
Strong back! Good leg! Fat for feast. Hold up, no drop feast!
Cage first. Question later. Mostly no question.
Get long pole. He too heavy for four.
Drag by hair. Hair for dragging.
Feet first. Always feet first. Head for Wizard.
Pick up before he cool. Cold meat for dogs.
Look at hands! Hands good eating.
Tie ankle. Tie wrist. Tie tongue, if he have one.

say: Shiny dhings! Boots! Teeth! Boots first. Dhen teeth.
I take his /CANNIBALCOIN/ and coat. He take nodhing, never again. Fair, no?
Look, look, little knife! Little knife for little cut!
Pretty! So pretty! Ring for ear, ring for nose, ring for pot!
Take bag. Take shoe. Take hair.
Nobody need two kidney and ring. Only one good for soup.
Leave bones. Ground eat bones bedder dhan us.
Keep cloth! Cloth clean knife. Cloth is fancy.
Give me shiny stick! No, mine!
Coins! /CANNIBALCOIN/! What dhey buy? Teeth? We have teeth.

say: Mm. Mmmm. Nnngh. Fat go all down chin, look.
Crunch. Crunch. Slurp. Ah, marrow best.
Hm. Dhis one was baker. You can tell. Floury.
Mmmmm! Knee best part. Knee, knee, lovely knee.
Chew chew chew. Swallow. Chew chew chew.
No talk. I listen to belly sing.
/CANNIBALHA/. Little /CANNIBALTOUGH/ today. Still. Still, still.
Hot! Hot! Hot! Blow on it. No burn tongue. Tongue for later.
Mmm, he was farmer. Salty from sweat. Sweet from grain.
Pass gravy. No, not dhat gravy. Odher gravy.
Hunger! Hunger! Fill pot! Fill pot, fill belly!
KA KLE LEK! Bring meat! Soft meat and string meat!
Gran' Wizard speak and bones listen. Hear bones? Bones laughing.
Hunger above, hunger below, hunger in belly, hunger in bone!
Fill pot and pot fill us! Feed us, feed us, feed us!
We feed, we fed. We eat, we eaten. Round, round, round dhe pit.
Paint red for feast. Every finger.
Red is colour. Red is way. Red is road to Hunger mouth!
Wizard say belly never full. Of course belly never full!
Belly small. Hunger big. We make up difference with neighbours.
They counted us again this morning. They counted me twice. I think it means soon.
Sixteen cages. I'm in the fourth. The first three are empty now.
I keep waiting to wake up. It's the cooking smell. It gets worse every day.
The one beside me stopped talking yesterday. I think he's lucky.
I used to count the days. Now I count the bones in the corner.
Please. I have a family. I have a... I have a horse. I'll give you the horse.
They come at dusk with the long poles. They pick. I pray it's never me and then I hate myself for praying.
I heard them sharpen the knives this morning. They sing while they do it. It's a very cheerful song.
They bring the water before they bring the knife. I think the water is for me. I think it's a kindness.
The man in the next cage bit through his own finger to get free. He didn't get free.
Nooo! Not the pot! Not the pot, please, I have a...
AAAH! They're cutting! They're cutting and they're ALIVE for it!
Somebody, anybody, kill me, finish it, anything but the fire!
Not my leg! I need the leg! I need it to run!
Mama! MAMA! They are coming with the pot!
Let me out! I'll tell you everything! I don't know anything! LET ME OUT!
Mother! Mother! I'm here! MOTHER!
Hit me, hit me, do whatever you like, but don't look at me like that!
I'll be good! I'll be good!
They're counting my ribs! They're counting my ribs! They've counted them twice!
You came back. You came. They said nobody ever does. Open it, open it, open it.
Quiet. Quietly. They're asleep. If they wake we're all dessert.
I don't care who you are. I'll carry your bags the rest of my life. The lock, please, the lock!
Key! The key's on the hook by the door! Hurry, hurry, they come at dawn!
I'll cut my own arm off if it gets me out. Oh, please don't make me.
Thank you. Thank you. Don't tell me what's in the pit.
Oh gods. Oh gods, thank you. Thank you. I thought I had imagined you.
Run. Don't wait for me. I'll follow. I'll follow as best I can.
I have no words. I have no words at all. Just let me hold your sleeve.
Never come back here. Never ever come back. Promise me. Promise me.
/CANNIBALHA/! Who brave now? Everybody taste brave inside.
Pick up. Careful. Soft ones first. Strong ones keep till winter.
You hit hard. You fall soft.
Ho ho! Strong fight, weak feed! Strong feed also. Later.
Stack like firewood. Careful, careful. Still resh.
Hee! One more for Gran' Wizard. One more for pot.
Should bring more friends. Friends is portions.
Dhis one scratch my face! Peel it!
Wake dogs. Dogs want taste. Not big taste.
/CANNIBALCURSE/! You hit hard, little meat.

say: AIEEEEE! AIEEEEE! HUNGRY! HUNGRY HUNGRY!
FLOOOP! FLOOOP! MEAT! MEEEAT!
EEEEK! EEEEK! AIYAAAH! FLOOOOP!
HUNGRY! HUNGRY! AIEEEEE!
EEEEE! HEAD! HEEEAD!
AAAAGH! AAAAGH! COME! COME COME COME!
SHEEE! SHEEEE! TEETH! TEEEEETH!
AIEEE! FLESH! FLEEEESH!
GRRAAAAH! NOW! NOW! NOW NOW NOW!
IIIIEEEE! BITE! BITE BITE BITE!
MINE! MINE! MINE MINE MINE!
SHINY! GIVE! GIVE GIVE GIVE!
MMMMM! MMMM! SNIFF! SNIFFFF!
BRIGHT! BRIGHT! EEEEE!
TAKE! TAKE! AIEEEE!
EEEE! EEEE! BONES! BONES!
HA HA HA HA HA HA!
AIYAAAH! AIYAAAH! EEEEK!
SMELL! SMELL! BLOOD! BLOOD! BLOOD!
LAUGH! LAUGH! HAHAHAHAH!
Hold still. I only need your measurements. Arm. Back. Chest.
Good hide. Even. Few scars. It would be a shame to waste it.
No need to run. Running bruises the stock.
You won't feel the first cut. You'll feel the rest, and that's the craft.
Such a good back. Straight, no scars. I'll be careful with it.
Your face. May I borrow it? It suits me.
I have a coat that needs a collar. You have a neck. Perfect.
Skin is cloth. You're a bolt of cloth that hasn't yet been cut.
I like the way you stand. It will look good on my wall.
Stop moving and I'll make it quick. Move, and I'll make it neat.

say: Hello. This is how you say hello. Yes. Hello.
You had a face once. We liked it.
Tall one. Pity. Tall ones need more thread.
Don't worry about the machines. They're only noisy at first.
What a lovely face. Have you ever thought of giving it away?
I am sorry. I am trying to listen politely. It is hard, with your voice so... wet.
Is that your own skin? Splendid. Most people wear someone else's.
Don't mind the stains on my apron. They're only stains.
Lovely weather for a fitting. Come to the house and we'll take your measure.
Everyone is a customer. Even the ones who don't know it yet.

say: A new bolt, unconscious, already smooth. Lift with care.
Take him back. Gently. If the surface bruises, we lose the front panel.
Delivered! Well, acquired. Delivery is a kind word for what happens to him next.
Fresh from the road and sleeping like a child.
Leave the clothes on until we are home.
Check his hands first. Hands are the finest work. Gloves from a good pair of hands go for a fortune.
He breathes. Good. The skin takes better when the heart is still ticking.
The hands are lovely. Look at the nails. Don't scratch them, whatever you do.
Rope on the ankles, a cushion for the head. Treat the new stock like a bride.
Cold hands, warm heart. Warm heart, warm hide. Take him home.
A new bolt, unconscious, already smooth. Lift with care.
Bring him to the peeler. Gently. If the surface bruises, we lose the front panel.
Delivered! Well, acquired. Delivery is a kind word for what happens to him next.
Fresh from the road and sleeping like a child.
Leave the clothes on until we're indoors. Mud ruins the pattern.
Check his hands first. Hands are the finest work. Gloves from a good pair of hands go for a fortune.
He breathes. Good. The skin takes better when the heart is still ticking.
The hands are lovely. Look at the nails. Don't scratch them, whatever you do.
Rope on the ankles, a cushion for the head. Treat the new stock like a bride.
Cold hands, warm heart. Warm heart, warm hide.
Take the clothes. Leave the bones. Wait. Is that a good scalp? I'll take the scalp.
Boots, belt, buckles. Don't scratch the leather. The leather is the whole point.
This one has a lovely birthmark. Cut around it. We will frame it.
Hat, boots, gloves. All of them very well made. Better than the person was.
Cut around the ear first. The ear is delicate. The rest is plain labour.
Odd. People carry so many things they'll never need. Skin is all anyone really wears.
Leave the nails on. Leave the teeth in. The buyers like a complete set.
Do not tear the shirt. A shirt fits another man just as well.
Oh, a pocket mirror. How thoughtful. I'll use it for a fitting.
The belt isn't good leather. The man was a different matter.

say: They bring a lamp when they come. I always know. They hold the lamp near my face first.
I counted the hooks on the ceiling. Twelve.
Please. Please don't tell me how many fit in one coat.
The machine runs all night. It hums. I think it hums a tune, and I hate that I know the tune now.
They measured me for something today. I didn't ask for what. I didn't need to.
They're so polite. That's what I can't bear. They're so polite about it.
Someone is whimpering in the next room. It might be me. It's hard to tell.
They said I have a very fine neck. I didn't know whether to thank them.
I can hear them practising. Slicing the air, careful, careful, until the sound is right.
One of the others was taken yesterday. They brought back his shoes.
Stop! Stop it, stop it! Not my face, not my FACE!
It's cold! It's peeling and it's COLD! Oh please, oh please, oh gods!
Kill me! Please kill me, they're taking all of it!
Don't! Don't! It's cold! It's so cold!
They're sewing it onto someone else! I can feel it!
Why are you wearing my coat? Why are you wearing MY COAT?
AAAAAH! The skin! It is coming off in sheets!
I'll give you anything! I'll give you a name! I'll give you all my names!
Mother, it's not as bad as it looks. It's worse. It's much worse!
Please, a sip of water! Only a sip! I'll be so quiet!
Don't damage the merchandise. Lift. Gently.
Shall we measure now, or after you wake up? After.
You fought beautifully. The skin on your knuckles will make fine gloves.
Tuck the hands in. Mind the face. We're going to need all of it.
Hush now. You've had a long day. A longer one is coming.
Down is down. Down is good. Down keeps the hide even.
Down so soon. How graceful. Few fall without a mark.
Not a bruise on the chest. A pity to let it go to waste.
Make a note of the height. I will draw the pattern in the morning.
Careful. Do not wake him. A quiet client is a happy client.

say: Order came in for six pairs of boots. Six, in one week. Nobody told me it was a rush.
I wore a woman's face to market once. Nobody noticed.
Savant says the cut is a form of love. I say the cut is an invoice.
We find the best hides in the Pits and the worst in the Ashlands. Ashlands skin is full of ash. Terrible stuff.
The last tanner I had drank cheap and sewed fine. Retired to the Skinhouse.
Something was wrong with the last batch. Nervous. Nervous leather is thin leather.
We have no time for songs. The machine hums enough.
Wore a Shek's coat once. The stripes wouldn't come off. The stripes are still on the coat.
They ask if we're lonely. We have so much company. Everyone brings their own face.
The knives need oiling. Not the metal. The leather handles. Every one is a hand.
Mmm. Mm. The fog says hello. The fog says you are tall.
Come inside. No. Do not. Come, come.
Here. Here. Here is the one.
Sing with us. Sing. Sing. Song for the meat.
The fog is hungry. You are tall.
We hear you. We hear your heart. It is very loud. It is going to be quiet.
AAAAH! AAAAH! LOOK! LOOK! UP! UP!
Walk, walk, walk toward the song. The song is warm. The song loves you.
Meat sings in the mist. Sing, meat, sing for your supper.
Mmm. Many voices. One heart. We hear it. Boom. Boom.
Mm. Mm. Mm. Do not be afraid. The fog loves you. It is going to love you very much.
Lost, are you? Good. Good lost.
Stay. Stay. The fog is warm once you are in it. Mm.
Lost, lost, lost. Come. The fog will find your road. It has found so many.
Stay, stay. The mist is a blanket.
Hum with us. Hm. Hm. The tune is easier from the inside.
Hush. The Prince is dreaming. Dream with him.
Mmm. Everyone is welcome in the fog. The fog likes company. It keeps what it likes.
Do not be afraid of the dark. The dark is only the fog with its eyes shut.
Come close. Closer. Hm. Warm. You are so warm.
Down. Down. He is down. Pole, pole, pole.
Meat sleeps. Meat dreams. Hush. We carry the dream.
Mm. Mm. Do not wake the prize. The prize wakes later, when the Prince arrives.
One down. One down. Carry the quiet one to the poles.
Fell, fell, fell. He fell asleep. We keep the sleeping ones.
Warm. Warm. Still warm. Quick, before the fog takes the warm.
One for the poles. One for the Prince. One for the fog. One for...
Pole is ready. Pole has been ready for days. Bring the sleeper, bring him now.
Mm. Warm still. The Prince will like him, Prince likes the warm ones.
Sleepers are best. Sleepers do not scream until the last.
Mmmm. Nnn. Mmm. Wet and slow, wet and slow.
Schlp. Schlp. Hm. Chew, chew, hum.
Aaaah. Ahhhh. Yes. So good. So bright.
Mm. Chew, chew. The fog chews with us. Mm.
Hhh. Hhh. Warm. Salt. Good.
Mm. Mm. Do not stop. Do not stop. The fog is watching and the fog is pleased.
Hhh. Mmm. It is still looking at me. Good. That is how you know it is fresh.
Mm. Still warm.
Slurp. Slurp. Yes. It looks at me still. Good eyes.
Do not waste it. Do not leave it for the mist. The mist is greedy.
Hail the pole. Hail the one on the pole. Hail the one who will be on the pole.
The Prince eats. We keep the song.
Round the stake. Round, round. Drop a bone for the fog.
Prince of the fog, Prince of the hum, Prince of the pole. Hear us.
Mm. Mm. Mm. We are small. The fog is big. The Prince is bigger.
He screams so well. So wide. The fog drinks it.
Do not look away. If you look away it is rude. It is very rude.
Sing the long song. Sing the long, long song. It has no end. That is its beauty.
Round the pole, round the pole. One more circle and he screams. One more circle.
Hum. Hum. The fog is listening.
Shiny. Shiny. Shiny for the pole. Hang it. Hang it.
Boots. Pretty boots. Pretty, pretty, pretty. Wear them on the poles.
Bits and pieces. Pieces and bits. Mmm. He will not need them in the fog.
Shiny for the poles. Shiny for the Prince.
Bones for the stakes, cloth for the flags, boots for the walkers.
Coin. Coin. We do not know coin. We know sparkle.
Pretty. Pretty. Hang it up. Hang it high where the Prince can see.
Teeth. Teeth are for the necklace. Teeth hum when the fog is near.
Give it here. No, here. It belongs to the fog. It always belonged to the fog.
Rings! Rings on the ears, rings on the stakes!
The poles. Oh god, the poles. They sing. They sing at us. They put us up and they sing.
I can hear one of them humming. A prince, I think. It's humming a lullaby.
Wake up, wake up, wake up. Please wake up. Please. It is not a dream.
I heard the Prince walk by. I heard him stop. He didn't choose me. Today he didn't choose me.
They stood over me and hummed. Then they left. I don't know which was worse.
I can see the others. They are so quiet. Their eyes are still open. Why are they looking at me?
The fog tastes of copper. I can't stop swallowing it.
They hum and the humming gets inside you. I'm humming now.
They haven't touched me yet. They're waiting. I don't know what for.
I counted eleven poles. Eleven. I'm on the eleventh. That's a good number. Is it a good number?
It's chewing! It's CHEWING! Make it STOP!
No! No! Not alive! Not while I'm still alive!
They are humming! Why are they humming, why are they humming, why!
Somebody help! Somebody, please, I'm still alive! Still alive!
It's inside! It's inside me! GET IT OUT!
Help! Help! Gods, somebody HELP! HELP!
I can still feel it! I can still feel all of it!
I can hear them humming! They're humming while they do it!
Please, please, kill me! End it!
STOP! STOP! STOP! STOP!
If you're heading north, take fire and a friend.
The nightmares do not stop. We keep killing. We keep killing anyway.
Count your party twice at dawn. If the number changes in the night, do not go looking.
If you're going north, carry salt. Burn what you can't carry.
Never fight them in the grass. Fight them at the edge of the fire, where they hesitate.
They look like us from far. They smile like us. Up close, they have teeth like pickets.
I have a brother's name carved on my boot. I haven't found the rest of him yet.
Do not go near the cages. Do not go near the cages. I mean it. You will want to.
They knew my name before I'd given it. That was how I learned to stay quiet.
I've seen what they do to the children. I can't unsee it. I'm hunting because of it.
I have burned four villages and I can't get the smell out of my cloak. Keep your distance, friend. I carry the north in my clothes.
If you hear singing in the grass, don't sing back.
I keep a list of the names I could save. It's very short. It's very short and getting shorter.
I'm not asking you to join. I'm asking you to know what's out there.
Take my advice. Go home. Take my second advice: you won't.
The tribes aren't one thing. They're many small things, all hungry, all at war. That's why they don't simply swallow the world.
Some of us do it for revenge. Some of us do it because the cages need emptying. All of us do it because we can't stop.
If a Hunter offers you a drink and refuses one himself, don't take it personally.
A knife is for work. A friend is for company. A cannibal is for neither.
I'll tell you what they fear: fire, iron, and a face that does not blink.
I found a boy once, still tied, still talking. He talked for a week. Then he stopped. I don't like quiet any more.
My captain says fear is the beginning of good sense. Then he drinks until he can't feel it.
I buried my last partner in a sack. Only half of him fit. I buried the half that fit.
Everybody has a reason for doing this job. Mine is that I haven't found a reason to stop.
My boots have a name carved in the sole. Not mine. A friend's. I walk on it so that I remember.
The Fog Islands lie just off the Gulf. Some nights you can smell them from the walls, and the walls are a long way off.
A paladin on the Gulf wall told me the fog makes a sound before it moves. Like a lot of people breathing in. Then it moves.
Our patrols come back two short. They say the missing wandered. Wandered where? Into the Gulf? With their boots on?
I saw a Deadhive Overrun once, from a hill. A whole town, standing. Doors open. Nothing moving. Nothing. I went home and prayed until I forgot the sight.
The Flame burns, and the Fog hungers. Don't ask which one the Holy Lords fear more.
They say the Fogmen were Hivers once. Beasts that lost their masters. Okran preserve us, if beasts go wrong like that, imagine men.
Every garrison near the Gulf keeps a torch lit at the gate all day. In the sun. Without a word, as a rule.

A pilgrim came back from the Gulf with his hair white. He said nothing. He never said anything again.
Hivers who wandered into the mist were never seen again. Their song still comes back on the wind.
Painted tribes in the north, past Okran's Valley. Heathens who eat the heretics before the Inquisition can. A grim kind of competition.
My cousin's patrol found a camp in the Valley. A cage, eleven skulls, a small one. They burned it down and still did not sleep for a month.

A trader swore the tribes have a book. A book of names. It has pages enough for all of us.
Out on the northern road, we found a cart with the horse still in the traces. No driver. No blood.

Machine heretics wearing flesh. If one of them comes near the altar, I will pray in their ear before I strike.
There is a house in the south that no pilgrim returns from. The Inquisition has stopped sending priests.

Machine heretics who wear human skin. Not even the Flame has a word for it.

Tengu pays well for caravans through Bast, and those caravans pay badly for it. Last month, one went missing in full. Wagons too.

We have a bounty on the Gran' Wizard. Forty thousand. I wouldn't take it for four hundred thousand.
A merchant came back from the Northern Coast with no cargo and no tongue. He still writes beautiful menus.
The Cannibal Hunters go out from the Bastion and half of them don't come home. The other half don't come home either.
Rebel Farmers pray the tribes don't go east. We pray the Farmers don't go west. Everybody lives in a small, quiet terror.
Heft won't send a patrol north of Bast. Taxes still go north. Isn't that interesting?
A cannibal chief once demanded a cut of the Guild's trade. The Guild paid in lead, delivered fast.
Merchants say they hear drums in the north every third night. They say the drums count down.

Brink's watch dragged three bodies out of the Pits last season. No skin. Not a mark on the bones. Whoever did it was patient.
Skinless corpses and a wanted poster for somebody called Savant. The poster has no face. The clerks don't know the face. Don't ask the clerks.
Eighty thousand in cats on a madman. No one wants to collect. They want to be somewhere else.
My uncle saw a coat once, in the Forbidden Zone, still wet. He left his own beside it and walked home cold.
A clerk in Brink counted eighteen pairs of boots left by the road last year. Eighteen, all unlaced. He keeps the count in a drawer.
There's a tale that skeletons make hides into clothes. Foolishness. Folk need something frightening in the south, I suppose.
Some say the skinners are skeletons. Some say they're men. The Guild has a standing reward for proof of either.
Eighty thousand cats on a face nobody has seen. A poster of an empty circle. A clerk's idea of a joke.
I buy leather for my shop and I no longer ask where it comes from.
An unpleasant business, the skin trade. The Guild declined to regulate it.
Berserkers are a shame we can bear. Painted flatskins aren't. A people who eat their own, whose honour is a pot.
In the Spider Plains we found a Shek and four flatskins on poles. Their eyes were still wet. I took my sword in two hands. I didn't lay it down for a week.
Skinners hunt the Roam. Not warriors, not men. Tailors. I'd face a thousand Hundred Guardians before one tailor.
Kral's Chosen boast that they fear nothing. They've never been to the Roam.
The Stone Golem does not guard the north. We know. That is why the north is full.
They take the dead from the border without ceremony. No pyre, no sand, no name. That is how a Shek knows the north is wrong.
Don't die in the Roam. If you must, die near a cliff, where there's no road for the body.

We do not go north. The sand there is not ours and it does not like Shek feet.
The ancestors say the Roam is cursed. The ancestors are right. They're also dead and safe.
We had a city. We had walls. The tribes ate the walls, then the people, then the city. We're what's left of the pot.
The painted ones come down to the shore at low tide. We sleep in boats. We sleep in shifts. We don't talk about the children.
The painted ones wait past the last light. Stray from the village and you're theirs. We say it like a prayer now.

Another family left last night. By boat, at dusk, with nothing but the children and a lamp.
I can't fish and not think of fishing nets. Do you know what they use them for?
When a stranger arrives, we count the strangers and we count ourselves. Then we count the strangers again.
They come by night and they don't knock. We bar the doors anyway, so they know we're still here.
I used to sing to my daughter. She asks me not to, now. She says the singing carries.
We bury nothing now. What the tide returns, it returns on its own terms.
The fog is thinner at dawn.

They said Mongrel keeps itself free. Free of everything but the hunger outside.

Nobody leaves Mongrel at night. The ones who do come back wrong, or not at all.
I stopped sleeping facing the window. I stopped sleeping.
Every time a caravan leaves, I count how many walk out. Every time one returns, I count again. Don't ask me the numbers.
Keep your shutters closed and your eyes on the floor. That's the rule of the town, and the rule of the town is the only rule.
Word is, the fog has a memory. I think it has a stomach.
Every dawn I count the lamps on the wall. Every dawn there are fewer. I don't know who lights them.
The painted tribes are our best fence. No sensible army will come close. We keep our own supply lines tight and stay out of the grass.
They killed three of our couriers last winter. We punished them. They ate the punishment. Now we don't punish them.
The Hidden Forest is not hidden from them. Only from the soldiers.
Some of us have started wearing bells. The bells scare off wolves. The tribes like bells. Bells mean something is walking.
We slip through the trees where the tribes can't. The trick isn't to be hungry.
I'm not afraid of dying. I'm afraid of what they'll say about it after.
A ninja who flinches is a ninja who's dead. I flinched once. I'm still deciding if I'm alive.
The tribes learned to leave us alone. We learned to leave them out of our songs.
My best friend went to scout the clearing. We sent a rope after him, then a prayer, then a stone.
If you see a lantern in the wood, do not follow it. If you see two, run.
Ashlands expeditions never come back. We call them expeditions to keep the funding. We call the survivors a rumour.
Stone-Head, the last of the Ashland Drifters, told one story about a friend named Cobby. Halfway through he stopped. He sat there for ten minutes.
Machinists argue the painted tribes are devolved humans. I say they are what humans do when nobody is looking.
Don't take a contract north of the Coast. Don't take one for Sonorous Dark at any price. Both ends are full of ghosts, and not the quiet kind.
Take a contract near the Plains and you get paid. Take a contract near the Plains and you get eaten.
I once found a skinned Tech Hunter in the Pits. He still had his goggles on. I took the goggles. I'm not proud. I wear them every day.
The old machines have no taste for flesh. That's the one mercy of the ash.
Whatever's under the ash is older than the Empire. Old things have long appetites.
We found a whole Tech Hunter camp once. Warm coals, warm stew, no people.
I like my work. Gold, scrap, a decent name.
We free slaves because the alternative is worse. Then you hear about the Skinhouse, and slavery starts to look like a promotion.
Spring has the only honest watch in the south. We counted nineteen skinless corpses in a single year. We buried them in coats.
Savant takes the ones who are already running. That's the terrible joke. He takes the ones who ran.
We could mount a raid. We could. Then who would eat our porridge? Nobody wants to think about who would eat what.
The chains we break are small things beside what the skinners do to a man.
Someone has to say a prayer for every body. We say it quickly. We aren't proud of how quickly.
Every rescue is a gamble. Some nights we pull out five. Some nights we pull out the skin of five.
I never speak the name Savant at dinner. Not out of fear.
I've held a man who asked to be killed. I did it. I have not been the same since.
When a slave tells you the Skinhouse is better, you stop arguing with them.
Skinners aren't bandits. Bandits want your coin. Skinners want your coat and what's under it.
We raid the pits. We pick fights with our own. Then we go home. Skinners don't go home. They're home.
Don't leave a wounded friend alone near the Roam. Don't leave a wounded enemy either.
I heard the skin bandits are Skeletons. Skeletons or not, I want no part of what they do.
I raid. I rob. I don't wear my enemies. There are limits even for thieves.
I've seen a raider cry once. He had been to the Skinhouse. He said nothing, just cried. I gave him my cloak and told him to forget.
There's a code, you know. You don't kill a man for his coat. You kill him for his gold. Then you take the coat.
My cousin joined the Skinned Ones. He says it's quiet work. I haven't seen him since.
Some of us aren't even afraid of dying. Some of us are afraid of the process.
Nobody dares the Roam in a good coat. Everybody leaves in a worse one.
The Fogmen are our cousins. The ones who lost the thread. We hear them sometimes in the Queen's hum, like a wrong note that never ends.
If the Queen falls, the village goes grey. Then the village goes to fog. We do not say this often.
A drone doesn't fear death. A drone fears the silence where the Queen was. The Fogmen live in that silence, eating it.
Some mornings I wake and listen to the hum. I'm afraid of the day it isn't there.
Our Queen weeps for her lost children in the fog. We cannot reach her tears.
We have kinsmen to the west who do not hum any more. Pray for them.
I met one of the fog-gone once. Quiet. Staring. He said my name, my true name, and then he cried.
We keep the song close. If we lose the song we lose the way home.
I dream of the fog. The fog dreams of me. Neither of us enjoys it.
Pray for the unhummed. They suffer more than anyone knows.
You have been north, heretic? I can smell it. Smoke and grease. Stand upwind of the temple.
If you carry the stink of the Fog Islands into a holy town, you will be burned for it. Wash first. Burn your coat.
Don't tell me what you saw. I have my own sleep to guard.
The Flame keeps us. Without it, the Fog and the painted tribes would sit at our table. Tell me, traveller, was the north bad?
You smell of the unclean. Stand back, and speak of nothing you've seen.
North of the Valley is a ditch where the Flame doesn't reach. Pray you don't fall in.
I have seen what the tribes do to pilgrims. If you are a pilgrim, I pity you. If you are a heathen, I pity them.
Did you pass the Plains? Then you are filthy in more ways than one.
The north is a sin that feeds on its own sin. Pray you did not bring any home.
If you carry anything from that land, leave it at the gate. If it is alive, leave it twice.
If you came through cannibal country or the Pits, you look it. No, don't tell me which.
If you were out on the Plains, I hope you were insured. Nobody insures against the Plains. The underwriters died of the shock.
Scrub up before the next city, peasant. You smell of woodsmoke and recent bad news.
There's a bounty on the Gran' Wizard and on Savant. Wanted posters, no faces. Do you know either? No? Good.
You have the look of someone who made a poor investment. Let me guess. The north?
Those who come back from the north are never quite the same. They stop haggling.
The Guild would pay for information on the northern routes. But I'd advise you to be vague.
Insurance, my friend, doesn't cover some places. Don't inform the clerk.
I suppose you saw things you won't describe. Good. I don't pay for nightmares.
Whatever you did up there, keep the receipts out of sight.
Flatskin, you walk like one who has been in the Roam. I don't ask. I only wish you luck you don't have.
Your eyes are too wide. That is the look of a warrior who saw something that did not fight back.
The Stone Golem sees all. It didn't look at what you have seen.
Don't tell me your tale. A Shek's ear doesn't need your nightmares.
The Stone Golem would ask what honour you left in the north. I will not ask. I do not wish to hear.
If you came from inland, and alone, that's either brave or you're already someone's dinner and haven't noticed.
Don't light a fire after dark. They follow the smoke.
I will sell you fish. I will not sell you directions.
A stranger on foot, alone. Either you're brave or you're bait.
Show your hands. Hands tell the truth. Faces lie.
If you hear your name from the grass, don't answer. If you hear it twice, run.
If you see someone you used to know, look away. They aren't who they were.

Do you hear the drums? Not yet? Then you haven't been here long.
Stay in the light. Stay in the open. Stay away from the water at night.
Fog Islands? You're alive. That's one of the better jokes of the week. Stay in Mongrel until your hands stop shaking.

Your pupils are huge. You have heard them humming. Sit. Drink. We don't talk about the hum here.
Don't tell the children what you saw. We tell them it was a bad dream. It's better if it stays a bad dream.
You went in and came out. Do you know how few can say that? Drink.

You smell of the north. Wash before you come near the village, if you can stand to be seen.
Hunters, tribes, ninjas. In the Hidden Forest, all the shadows have knives. Mind which ones are friends.

If you saw anything in the dark with too many fingers, don't mention it. The ninjas are sensitive.

Nobody carries anything useful out of there. If you did, don't tell me.
Look at me, friend. Your eyes are red. Whatever you saw is in them.
You have the glaze of someone who has walked into the wrong thing and out the other side.
If you picked up any tech in that place, put it down.

Another one back from the dark. Come, there's soup, and you can tell me nothing.

Fresh from the Plains? Count your fingers, and your friends.

You've been in the red grass. The look in your eye tells me. Take a drink and a seat.

Up north there are people who will eat you. Not metaphorically. I asked a clerk, and he laughed, and then he stopped laughing.
A trader told me the Cannibal Plains are thirty days' walk across and fifteen of them are screaming.

Cats don't matter in the north. No one trades.

Fogmen. Skinners. Painted ones. Do they have a guild? Because that's a lot of competition for us criminals.
Heard a rumour about a house made of skin. I laughed. I laughed a lot. Then I went outside and was sick in the alley.
Whoever's been wearing faces in the south, they ain't bandits. Bandits want your cash, not your cheeks.
Up north they eat people. Course they do. Down here we only sell them.
Big boss says never take a job north of the Hook. I never asked why. I don't ask follow-up questions in this life.
Folk say the north's got a hunger so old it forgot it was a hunger. It's just there, like weather.
Everybody knows a man who knows a man who got eaten. Nobody knows the man who got eaten.
Some fella tried to sell me a bracelet made of knucklebones. Said it was lucky. I punched him.
I don't care how hard you are. You go into the Pits, you come out thinner.
A caravan came from the north with half the guards it started with and a full cargo it wouldn't open.
Our elders say that when the sun goes down in the north, something rises to take its place. They don't say what.

A merchant tried to sell me a lantern from the north. It would not stop humming.
The old nomads say there's a place where the sand has teeth. Never go there, my grandmother said. Never go, not even to look.
Black cloud, red fog, men like stitched dolls. A traveller told me. I gave him a bed. He didn't wake up.
If you see a man smiling with a face that doesn't belong to him, don't smile back. That's all the advice I have.
I met a man who had walked out of the fog. His beard was white and he was twenty.
In our tongue the northern fog has a name that means the mouth. We don't speak it aloud.
I thought I was hard. Then a Hunter drank at my table and told me one story, one, and I paid for his drinks for a month.
Starving men say they would eat their own boots. Up north they do worse.
Hungry? Be glad you're only hungry. In the north they're hungry for you.
Selling slaves is a trade. Selling them to the Plains is a funeral.

I heard that a man can lose his face in the south and never miss it until he looks in a puddle.

Some say all history is a pile of bones. They didn't say whose.

If you've come from somewhere awful, I won't ask. I'll only buy you a drink if you promise not to say.

They say if you hear a lullaby at midnight, it's already too late. I never sleep at midnight.
Never trust a stranger with a smile that stays in the same spot. I learned that the hard way.
There's a look people get when they come back from the north. You have it. Like a coin that has been boiled.
I've been to a lot of places and I've never wanted to be sick as often as when someone talks about the north.
The north changes people. I'm told it does the opposite of what you'd expect. It makes them very polite.
I've got a friend who went north and wrote me one letter. It was blank.
I was told stories about the Cannibal Plains and the Fog. I laughed. Now I see you and I'm not laughing.
One traveller told me he saw a house built of faces. I asked what the faces were made of. He started to cry.
Please don't tell me where you've been. The mere thought gives me gooseflesh.
Somebody told me a story about a whole village that vanished overnight. Pot still on the fire.
They say folk in the north eat the unwashed.
Stay in the road. Lock your door. Count your children. That's all that I know about the north.
They say the north tastes of iron and the south of dust. They also say it tastes of us.
