The Wizard has never been seen to blink. They say he counts his meals, and the numbers are in the millions.
If you're caught, don't beg the Wizard. He likes begging. It adds a note to the stew.
He sits at the top of a hill of bones, and every bone is a name he remembers.
They say the Wizard talks to the dead in his sleep and the dead answer. I'd rather not know what they say.
Never offer him a gift. Never accept one. Never, ever shake his hand.
The Plains are his, from the coast to the cliffs. Everyone else is just passing through his larder.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: There's a king of the cannibals. A wizard. Sits on a throne of bones. Why would anyone make that up? I can't imagine.
I heard his teeth are made of gold. I heard he swallowed a priest whole. I heard a lot of things, none of them nice.
The Gran' Wizard! I know that name. Mothers say it in the swamps when children won't sleep.
They say the cannibal king keeps a throne of skulls. They say every skull is labelled. Imagine the paperwork.
The Wizard has a fire that never goes out. The fuel is, I hear, quite varied.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard imprisoned by player

say: Wizard in cage. Wizard in CAGE! Who put Wizard in cage? Who have key?
We hear him call. We cannot go. Key walk away with stranger.
Somewhere cage hold Wizard. We run out of names for stranger. All names taste same.
Wizard chained. Pot cold. Who tell us what eat? Who tell us who eat?
Key gone. Wizard gone. We stand at fire. Nobody dare add wood.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard imprisoned by player

say: Somebody has the Cannibal Grand Wizard in chains. In chains! The bounty is forty thousand. I wouldn't touch the chains.
I heard he stares at the guards and says each of their names slowly, as if tasting. The guards asked to be rotated.
If the Wizard rots in a cell, the Plains will be quiet for a season. After that, they'll be worse.
The Wizard has been captured. The border is on edge. The Hunters have sworn to guard the road with their lives.
A caged king is a dangerous thing. The tribes will pay anything to get him back. Anything.
Meat Lord down. Who next Meat Lord? Not me. Not me, not me, please.
Chiefs stand round empty pit. Nobody brave enough to sit.
First Village quiet. Quiet is bad. Quiet mean somebody plan. Somebody always ungry.
Meat Lord fall. Ground shake. I feel in bones. Dhen I feel in bones I am next.
We make fire for him. No catch. Make anodher.
Meat Lord, down at First Village. Thirty thousand cats from three nations. The man who did it will never need to pay for a drink again.
They said he was too strong to kill. They said a lot of nonsense. Then somebody walked up and did it.
We went to the First Village after, and counted the Chiefs. Some ran, some wept. Wept!
The Meat Lord is dead. They say the earth is lighter. They say the village is bigger now.
I'd have wept for a Hunter dead. I danced for the Meat Lord.
I'm told Meat Lord ate before any Chief and after any Chief.
People are already arguing about who gets his seat. It's the worst kind of inheritance.
They say Meat Lord ate like a pack of wolves. I've seen bigger appetites.
Nobody wants to be the next Meat Lord. They sleep with one eye open and a prayer in the other.
Word is, he died roaring. I'd have died quietly, but I'm not him.
Meat Lord. Big as a door, strong as a bull, and the Chiefs follow him like gulls follow a boat.
He says little. Meat Lord points and says take meat. Then a Chief or a victim goes in the pot. That's the whole law.
Thirty thousand on his head from three nations. Nobody has even got close enough to see the colour of his eyes.
Meat Lord has a voice like a barrel full of gravel. When he laughs, the pot rattles on the fire.
They say he can lift a man over his head and drop him in the pot in one move.
The master is gone. The master is gone. Who will cut the pattern now? I can't sew without a pattern.
The Skinhouse is empty. The coats have nobody to wear them. They hang, and sway, and I think they're listening.
Do you know how long it takes to learn the whole craft? Years. Now there's no one to teach it. We wear his things instead. Poor fit.
The house won't hold without him. The needles have dropped.
I looked for his apron in the cupboard. It was gone. I don't know who took it.
We were so careful. Always careful. And then, one day, one stranger, one little accident. And the master was in pieces.
He promised us immortality, in a way. We would all be worn by someone, eventually.
The master's chair is empty and nobody dares to sit in it. We take turns brushing the dust.
We kept his coat. It still smells of him. We'll wear it by turns.
Without him we're just people who like cutting. That isn't a calling.
You. You did that to the master. I know your hands. I'll wear your hands first.
The master is dead and so I'm free to choose any design I like.
I kept his scissors. Do you want to see how well they still cut?
I shall wear your skin to his funeral. It's the least I can do for the master.
Savant taught me to be patient. I've been patient for years.
You have a nice coat. It will be mine. It's already mine, I only wait for the person inside to finish.
You'll make a splendid memorial. Splendid.
Don't run. We have all night, and now we have no master to disappoint.
We kept his needles. We kept his gloves. Soon we'll keep your hands.
Your coat is nice. I'd have taken it anyway, but now I take it for him.
Savant is dead. A madman, a flayer, eighty thousand in cats, and he's dead. I won't ask who. I'll pay for the next three rounds.
People say the Skinhouse has fallen. The Southern Hive have come in to wash the walls. Someone should wash the ground, too.
I cut down one of his hangings once. A man, inside out, still talking. It took me three days to stop hearing it. Now the man who hung him is dead and I can almost sleep.
Skinless corpses in the Pits and all the signs say they're done. The patrols have stopped. The dust no longer smells of leather.
The skinner is dead. I am told the Roam smells of unpicked threads and spilled rum.
Someone did the world a favour. Someone I wouldn't want to meet in a hallway.
I don't believe in justice. I believe in a quiet Pits road and an empty Skinhouse.
They say his throne is empty. Someone should put a lamp in it. A lamp, and then a match.
The Southern Hive brought songs to the Roam. The songs frightened off the last of the ghosts.
It's not often you hear a fair piece of news. This is one.
The Skinhouse is cold. We wash the halls. We wash the faces off the walls.
The tailor isn't. We came in when the screaming stopped. We found what he kept.
He wore faces. We didn't understand.
The Roam is quieter. The hive hums over the dead of the Skinhouse.
Heard someone killed a madman called Savant. A skinner. I thought skinners were a story told to make children be good.
The United Cities announced the death of somebody wanted. A Savant. No face on the poster. I don't know who they killed.
I heard whoever killed the skinner is cursed. I say whoever killed the skinner deserves a drink.
The skinner's dead, people say. A good thing. It would have been a better thing earlier.
I hear the leather trade is in trouble. No more mysterious supplies. I find I don't mind.
You. You went to the Skinhouse and walked out. There are people who owe their children's sleep to you. Not many. Nobody knows.
I have a coat I'll never wear again. Thank you.
The tailor is dead. They say. If you killed him, I'd like to shake your hand. If you didn't, I'd like to shake your hand.
I saw the Skinhouse in a dream once. A tall house, and every window had a face. You're the one who put out the lights.
I have a cousin who disappeared in the Roam. If you saw him, don't tell me.
I won't say your name. I won't say it. But I'll say a prayer for the one who did it.
The Skinhouse is cold. That's thanks to you. I'd light a candle in your name, but you might not like the attention.
I wanted to say something. I have forgotten what. Walk on, friend, walk on.
People talk. They say a stranger ended the tailor. Whatever else happens, I won't argue.
You've the look of one who's done a thing no one else could. It's not a good look.
There's a madman named Savant who peels folk like fruit. The Cities have a poster of him with no face. A poster of nobody, for a man everybody fears.
Savant has a throne in a house of skins, I heard. And a bed. A very large bed. I'd like to leave it at that.
They call themselves the Skinned Ones. Imagine choosing that name. Imagine meaning it.
Eighty thousand cats. That's what a flayer fetches, if you can get close enough to count his fingers.
Word is, the tailor never sleeps and never hurries. He has a measured, patient voice, and he uses your name.
Nobody has ever described Savant's voice. Nobody who heard it was ever in the position to describe.
Savant has a signature, they say: a neat cut at the base of the neck. Neat.
The Cities have sent six squads after him. One came back. It carried a single glove.
If you meet a polite man in a mask in the Roam, you've met the man.
Word is, you can tell when you're near. The air gets drier. Your own skin starts to itch.
Folk say a skeleton in a man's face sells hides in the south. A Savant. They say he can tell what you're worth by squeezing your arm.
In the swamp they say there's a tailor who makes coats from the people who refused to pay. Nonsense. Nobody refuses to pay that tailor twice.
I heard of a house of skin. Don't ask me where. Don't tell me where.
I've heard of a skeleton who tailors folk into coats. It's a children's story, I think. Surely it's a children's story.
A madman in the south skins travellers and hangs the hides to dry. I'll take the long way round.
The master is chained. The master is being shown to the world. We cannot reach him. Oh, we cannot reach him.
They have the master in a cage. He's quiet. I fear the quiet more than the screaming.
Without his hands, the machines don't hum properly.
Our master is a prisoner. Without his voice the house goes cold and the needles forget their work.
Who will cut the pattern now? They've taken the master and left us tangled.
Savant is in chains. Someone has the flayer in chains. I'd pay to look at him. I'd pay twice not to be looked at back.
A jailed madman is a risk. He talks to the guards. They stop being guards. I don't know how else to put it.
Eighty thousand for him alive, I heard. I wouldn't take him alive, and I wouldn't take eighty thousand.
The skinner is caged. They say he hums to himself and the guards sleep poorly.
Savant is captured. For once the world has done a small, sane thing.
The tailor is held. We feel the Skinhouse waiting. We don't go in while he lives.
The man who wears faces is in a cage. He hums. Not our hum.
Caged, the skinner. Caged is better than free. It isn't better than not.
We watched the Skinhouse a long time. Now it watches nothing.
